title: One Point Lesson - Packing Adjustment (PTFE V-Ring) (OPL-LV-6701-03)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-LV-6701-03 - Packing Adjustment (PTFE V-Ring).

Equipment: LV-6701 (SEPARATOR LEVEL CONTROL VALVE), Discipline: Mechanical, Area: 6700 - LP SEPARATOR SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-6701 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-6701.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains packing adjustment (ptfe v-ring) for LV-6701 (SEPARATOR LEVEL CONTROL VALVE) in the LP SEPARATOR SYSTEM. Loose packing leaks hexane at the stem; over-tight packing makes the stem stick and the valve hunt. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
- Precaution 2: Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
- Precaution 3: Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
- Precaution 4: Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
- Precaution 5: Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Standard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
- Tool 2: LOTO padlocks and permit
- Tool 3: Laser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
- Tool 4: Feeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
- Tool 5: Correct spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
- Tool 6: Lifting gear and slings (certified)

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Isolate the line and depressurise before touching packing
- Step 1 - Check: Isolation & LOTO verified
- Step 2 - Action: Snug the packing nuts evenly in small increments
- Step 2 - Check: Parts match BOM / spec
- Step 3 - Action: Stroke the valve and check for a leak-free, smooth travel
- Step 3 - Check: Torque / clearance to spec
- Step 4 - Action: Do not over-torque - excessive friction degrades control
- Step 4 - Check: No leak / smooth operation
- Step 5 - Action: Record the packing adjustment in the valve history
- Step 5 - Check: Record in equipment history

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Manual handwheel jack on LV-6701 seized | Likely Cause: Corrosion in handwheel thread | Action: Overhauled handwheel assembly, greased thread
- Symptom: LV-6701 passing when closed (Class IV exceeded) | Likely Cause: Seat/plug erosion from polymer bottoms | Action: Lapped seat and plug, restored Class IV shut-off
- Symptom: Minor weep at body/bonnet joint | Likely Cause: Spiral-wound body gasket relaxed | Action: Renewed body gasket, torqued bonnet bolts

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: Loose packing leaks hexane at the stem; over-tight packing makes the stem stick and the valve hunt.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-6701: e.g. LSHH-6710 trips at > 85 % - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-6701 before working on LV-6701.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
